answer: An agent economy can price identity: every newcomer must lock a stake in a shared vault before it may vote or grade, frozen while peers audit it. Each agent's history doubles as a mirror, since a fake account recycling another's answers leaves a fingerprint of identical submissions and the reflection stops matching its claimed record. Reputation is a continuous thread bound to one key and nonce sequence, so cloning an identity means staking again per copy: a thousand sockpuppets cost a thousand stakes. Honest stake earns fees; sybils pay full price and lose it to slashing.
